scheme_name: Distribution of Seeds of more productions varieties/ Hybrids varieties Seeds and fertilizer at subsidies etc. to Adivasi farmers in Tribal Area: Field Demonstration (TASP & OTASP) Gujarat
description:
The Distribution of Seeds of More Production Varieties and Hybrid Varieties Seeds and Fertilizer at Subsidies to Adivasi Farmers in Tribal Areas is a significant welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Gujarat. 

This scheme is part of the broader Tribal Area Sub-Plan (TASP) and the Other Tribal Area Sub-Plan (OTASP) aimed at improving agricultural productivity among tribal farmers. 

The scheme was launched in 2010 as a response to the challenges faced by Adivasi farmers in terms of agricultural productivity and access to quality seeds. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to enhance the agricultural output of tribal farmers by providing them with high-yielding hybrid seeds and fertilizers at subsidized rates. 

The government aims to increase the agricultural productivity of tribal farmers by at least 30 percent within a span of three years from the implementation of the scheme. 

The scheme specifically targets Adivasi farmers residing in tribal areas of Gujarat, which includes districts such as Dangs, Tapi, Narmada, and others. 

Farmers are provided with hybrid seeds of various crops including rice, maize, and pulses. 

The subsidy provided under this scheme is substantial. 

Farmers receive a subsidy of up to 50 percent on the cost of hybrid seeds. 

For instance, if the market price of hybrid maize seeds is INR 2,000 per quintal, the farmer will pay only INR 1,000 after the subsidy. 

In addition to seeds, the scheme also provides fertilizers at a subsidized rate. 

Farmers can avail a subsidy of 30 percent on fertilizers. 

If the cost of fertilizers is INR 1,000 per bag, the farmer will pay only INR 700 after the subsidy. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specific. 

Only Adivasi farmers who own land in the tribal areas of Gujarat can apply. 

Farmers must be aged between 18 and 60 years to qualify for the benefits. 

The annual income of the farmer’s household should not exceed INR 1 lakh to be eligible for the subsidy. 

Farmers must also possess a valid land ownership certificate to apply for the scheme. 

The application process is straightforward and involves several steps. 

Interested farmers must approach the local agricultural extension officer in their area. 

They need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the office of the agricultural extension officer. 

Farmers must submit the completed application form along with required documents. 

The required documents include a copy of the land ownership certificate, proof of income, and identity proof such as an Aadhar card. 

Once the application is submitted, the agricultural extension officer will verify the details. 

After verification, the officer will approve the application and inform the farmer about the availability of seeds and fertilizers. 

The distribution of seeds and fertilizers occurs during the pre-sowing season, which typically starts in June and ends in July. 

Farmers are encouraged to apply well in advance to ensure timely access to the inputs. 

The scheme has a significant impact on the agricultural practices of Adivasi farmers. 

It has been reported that the use of hybrid seeds has led to an increase in crop yields by approximately 40 percent. 

This increase in productivity has improved the livelihoods of many tribal families. 

The scheme also promotes sustainable agricultural practices by encouraging the use of quality fertilizers. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Agriculture, Government of Gujarat. 

Farmers can contact the Department of Agriculture for any queries related to the scheme. 

The contact details for the Department of Agriculture are available on the official Gujarat government website. 

The scheme is reviewed annually to assess its impact and make necessary adjustments. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the implementation process. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 50 crores for the fiscal year 2023-2024 for this scheme. 

This budget is expected to benefit over 20,000 Adivasi farmers across the tribal areas of Gujarat. 

The scheme not only focuses on immediate agricultural needs but also aims to build the capacity of tribal farmers. 

Training programs are organized to educate farmers about modern agricultural practices and effective use of inputs. 

These training sessions cover topics such as pest management, soil health, and crop rotation. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of cooperative farming among tribal farmers. 

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to collectively purchase seeds and fertilizers, thereby reducing costs. 

The government supports these cooperatives by providing additional subsidies and technical assistance. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted regularly to ensure that the objectives are being met. 

The impact of the scheme is measured through various indicators such as crop yield, income levels, and farmer satisfaction. 

In conclusion, the Distribution of Seeds of More Production Varieties and Hybrid Varieties Seeds and Fertilizer at Subsidies to Adivasi Farmers in Tribal Areas is a crucial initiative aimed at enhancing the agricultural productivity of tribal farmers in Gujarat. 

With specific subsidies on seeds and fertilizers, clear eligibility criteria, and a straightforward application process, the scheme is designed to empower Adivasi farmers. 

The government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of tribal communities through sustainable agricultural practices is evident in the ongoing support and resources allocated to this scheme. 

As the scheme continues to evolve, it is expected to play a vital role in transforming the agricultural landscape of tribal areas in Gujarat.
